name: Federated governance

subjectOf.text: In the federated model of AI governance many challenges cannot easily be decentralized, because distinct entities maintain their own AI systems and datasets, producing variation in standards, protocols, and formats that obstructs a unified governance framework.
subjectOf.abstract: In the federated model of AI governance, many challenges cannot be easily decentralized. For example, different entities or organizations maintain their own AI systems and datasets. This can lead to variations in standards, protocols, and formats used
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance Via Web3 Reputation System (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4941807
scope_conditions: where separate organizations maintain independent AI systems and datasets

subjectOf.text: When decision making power is distributed across multiple entities in a federated model, consensus and cooperation become harder to reach, which makes cohesive AI governance mechanisms difficult to establish.
subjectOf.abstract: In a federated model, where decision-making power is distributed across multiple entities, it becomes harder to achieve consensus and cooperation, making it challenging to establish cohesive AI governance mechanisms.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance Via Web3 Reputation System (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4941807
scope_conditions: where governance authority is distributed across multiple independent entities

subjectOf.text: In a federated model transparency and accountability across all participating entities are hard to ensure precisely because there is no centralized control, and Kaal notes that he does not otherwise advocate such centralized control.
subjectOf.abstract: In a federated model, it can be challenging to ensure transparency and accountability across all participating entities due to the lack of centralized control, which this author does not otherwise advocate.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance Via Web3 Reputation System (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4941807
scope_conditions: in federated models lacking centralized control

subjectOf.text: Enforcing AI regulation in a federated model is complex because different entities may interpret the same regulations differently and may show differing levels of commitment to compliance.
subjectOf.abstract: In a federated model, enforcing regulations and policies related to AI can be complex. In a decentralized setting, different entities may have varying interpretations of regulations or differing levels of commitment to compliance.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance Via Web3 Reputation System (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4941807
scope_conditions: in decentralized settings with multiple independent compliance actors
